messages:
Alice W: Heads-up: noticed a regression on embeddings -> rerank path after today's kernel-selection change. p90 token-latency for rerank up from ~18ms -> ~36ms. QPS for the endpoint stayed flat.
Ben T: Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/embeddings-rerank — pulling graphs now.
Cara M: quick glance: token-level breakdown shows big jump in KV lookup time. KV::lookup doubled for long contexts.
Dinesh: Which model + vector dim? 768 vs 1024 matters for kernel choice.
Alice W: open-embed-1024-q4f in prod. vector_dim=1024. Typical rerank batch sizes are small (<=8), but overall pipeline uses batch_target=64.
perf-bot: [perf] kernel_fallback triggered on host gpu-12 at 1749001002. reason=aten_kernel_mismatch. affected_pct=17%.
Ben T: Can someone paste the profiler hot spots snippet from that window?
Cara M: ```
Profiler snapshot (1749001000..1749001100)
- KV::lookup             -> 11.2ms (was 4.7ms baseline)
- Attention_kernel       -> 6.1ms
- KernelSelection/Dispatch-> 3.0ms
- BatchPrep/IO           -> 1.4ms
```
Alice W: KV::lookup baseline was ~4.7ms on the previous kernel selection path. So large regression there.
Dinesh: Batching heuristics: rerank route has batch_limit=32 in route config, which can cause microbatch flushes when QPS low, making kernel switches more frequent. That interacts badly with kernel compile/fallback.
Ben T: The token-latency breakdown panel shows spikes specifically in 'kernel_selection' and 'kv_prepare' stacks during the incident window.
Eva L: perf-bot also flagged increased compile time for quantized kernels around that time.
Cara M: Additional note: we recently changed KV cache TTL in PR #422 (lowered to 5s) to reduce memory pressure — that could increase misses and amplify lookup cost.
Ben T: We should measure: per-route kernel_choice counter, batch_size histogram, kv_miss counter, kv_fetch_ms histogram, and tag metrics with vector_dim.
Alice W: Customer impact: two enterprise customers reported rerank p95 > 1.2s (from ~0.6s). Raising priority.
Sam R: Confirming PR #422 lowered TTL to 5s. It was intended for low-memory hosts. Rolling back TTL change now to 60s on canary hosts.
Dinesh: Mitigation options: 1) force policy=prefer_fast_kernels for /rerank route (avoid fallback), 2) tune batch_limit to avoid microbatches, 3) roll back TTL, 4) revert kernel-selection heuristic patch if needed.
Cara M: Caveat: forcing prefer_fast may bypass quantized path and increase cost. But for rerank latency SLA > cost here.
Ben T: I'll own adding the instrumentation panels and the per-route kernel_choice metric. Will add a batch_size histogram and vector_dim tag.
Alice W: I'll create a Console incident with notes and customer list, and add a canary rollout to force prefer_fast on a small percentage of traffic.
Sam R: Rolling TTL rollback now. Pushing change to canary cluster (canary id=c72).
Eva L: perf-bot: will resume alerting on kernel_fallback changes once metrics land.
Cara M: After rollback and canary, let's collect new profiler samples and compare: target metrics to capture: QPS, end-to-end p50/p90/p95, token-level p50/p90/p99, kv_miss_rate, avg_kv_fetch_ms, kernel_fallback_rate, batch_size_percentiles, per-batch latency.
Ben T: I'll also add an alert: rerank token p90 increase > 1.5x baseline -> paging.
Alice W: Action items:
- Sam: rollback TTL on canary (in progress).
- Ben: add kernel_choice, batch_size histogram, kv_miss, vector_dim tagging to metrics + dashboard panels.
- Ben & Cara: run profiler comparisons before/after canary.
- Alice: create incident ticket + customer comms + canary config to prefer_fast.
- Dinesh: review batching heuristics; consider changing route batch_limit for rerank to 8-16.
Ben T: I'll update the ticket with links when dashboards are ready.
Alice W: Thanks all. Please drop short status updates here as you make progress :thumbsup:
